The computable StructureDefinitions were primary. Narrative specification pages would improve confidence for the intended semantics of contained Parameters/additional resources and the dom-3 invariant rewrite.
No terminology expansion was needed for local DomainResource elements. Expansions would matter for inherited Resource.language, which is out of scope for this DomainResource report.

scope.scopeNotesMd: This report analyzes the local `DomainResource` artifact: the root `DomainResource` element and the locally defined `text`, `contained`, `extension`, and `modifierExtension` elements. The R6 StructureDefinition exists at the assigned path and has the same canonical URL, id, kind, abstract flag, type, base definition, and derivation as R4. Inherited `Resource` elements shown in the DomainResource snapshot (`id`, `meta`, `implicitRules`, and `language`) were reviewed only to separate them from local changes and are not reported as local findings.
outOfScope: Changes inherited only from `Resource`, including `Resource.id`, `Resource.meta`, `Resource.implicitRules`, and `Resource.language`, are excluded from `findings[]`.
The inherited `Resource.language` binding change visible in the DomainResource snapshot is a Resource-level issue, not a local DomainResource finding.

The `ele-1` constraint and other Element-level representation changes are owned by the Element report except where this report calls out the absence of XPath for the local DomainResource dom-* constraints.

The `ext-1` constraint placement and Extension value[x] type-domain changes are owned by the Extension report. DomainResource's `extension` and `modifierExtension` elements still have type `Extension` and unchanged local cardinality/slicing.

narrativeReportMd:
# DomainResource R4 to R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No direct local element removal, rename, cardinality tightening, type removal, reference-target change, or binding change was found for `DomainResource`. The material local risks are mostly runtime, validation, and semantic/conformance risks rather than ordinary old-valid/new-invalid instance breaks.

## Scope
The local DomainResource root and local elements `text`, `contained`, `extension`, and `modifierExtension` were compared. Inherited `Resource` and `Extension` changes were deliberately excluded from `findings[]` and listed out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The biggest implementation change is that `DomainResource.modifierExtension` is now marked as summary content, which can change `_summary` payloads and generated summary models. The local contained-resource invariant `dom-3` was rewritten in FHIRPath, so validators should regression-test contained-resource reference patterns. The R6 StructureDefinition no longer carries XPath expressions for the local dom-* invariants, which affects XPath-only validation tooling.

## Highest-impact findings
All findings are Medium or lower. None is a clear hard validation break from a local cardinality or type-domain change.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for the intended equivalence of the `dom-3` FHIRPath rewrite and for the R6 `contained` text around `Parameters` and additional resources, because the computable StructureDefinition alone does not fully explain the design intent.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most changes are probably justified as safety or tooling modernization. Less disruptive alternatives existed for transitional tooling, such as retaining XPath metadata or publishing official invariant test cases, but those alternatives would add maintenance burden.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the Resource report for inherited `Resource.language` and implicitRules changes, and the Extension report for `ext-1` placement and Extension value[x] type-domain changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `DomainResource` keeps its identity and local content model, with no local element removals or cardinality/type narrowing. The main concerns are changed summary serialization for `modifierExtension`, the rewritten `dom-3` contained-resource invariant, and semantic text changes for contained resources. Confidence is medium because official diffs, invariant test cases, and narrative pages were not available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration work should focus on validator and serializer behavior rather than structural data transforms. Existing instances that use `text`, `contained`, `extension`, or `modifierExtension` remain structurally representable, but summary-mode APIs and contained-resource validation should be regression-tested. Cross-version conversion should also document policy for R6 contained resources that are `Parameters` or R6-only/additional resource types.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for direct computable deltas in the two StructureDefinitions: identity, cardinality, types, slicing, flags, and local constraints were compared. Confidence is medium for semantic impact because the supplied inputs did not include official change notes, normative narrative pages, or conformance test cases proving whether the `dom-3` expression rewrite is behaviorally equivalent.

findings.title: DomainResource.modifierExtension is now included in summaries

oldState.summary: `modifierExtension` existed as `0..* Extension`, was a modifier, and was not marked summary.

flags.isModifierReason: Modifier extensions are expected to modify the meaning or interpretation of the resource that contains them

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `DomainResource.modifierExtension` was present and safety-significant, but `isSummary` was false in the DomainResource snapshot.

newState.summary: `modifierExtension` remains `0..* Extension` and a modifier, but is now marked summary.

flags.isModifierReason: Modifier extensions are expected to modify the meaning or interpretation of the resource that contains them

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `DomainResource.modifierExtension` is included in summary content. The field's cardinality, type, slicing, and modifier status are otherwise unchanged.

facts.note: The summary flag changed on a local DomainResource element.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements have the same element id, path, type, cardinality, slicing, and modifier flag; only summary-related metadata changed materially.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not make a full R4 instance invalid in R6. It can break runtime assumptions around `_summary`, generated summary DTOs, serializers, caches, or clients that compare summary payload shapes. R6 servers or serializers that honor `isSummary` may now include `modifierExtension` where R4 summary views did not.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Modifier extensions can change interpretation. Including them in summary output is safer clinically, but clients that previously ignored or did not model them in summary payloads may mishandle safety-relevant qualifiers.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure summary representations preserve modifier extensions that cannot safely be ignored.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `isSummary=false` and add a base narrative obligation or best-practice rule telling summary producers to include modifier extensions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal is reasonable: a summary view that drops resource-level `modifierExtension` can mislead consumers because modifiers change interpretation. The less-breaking design would preserve the old summary shape, but it would not meet the safety goal as reliably as a computable summary flag, so the breakage is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would leave `DomainResource.modifierExtension.isSummary` as `false` and add explicit conformance text or a best-practice rule that modifier extensions should be included in summary views. That avoids the R6 summary-shape change but creates a conflicting or less computable signal and increases the risk that implementations continue to omit modifiers.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 summary payload shape only by weakening the machine-readable signal; summary producers could still omit safety-relevant modifier extensions.

examples.examplesMd: A concrete DomainResource such as a Patient or Observation with a resource-level `modifierExtension` remains valid as a full resource in both versions. The behavioral difference appears when a server, serializer, or generated model produces a summary view: R6 summary output can include the modifier extension while R4 summary output would not include it based on this flag.

findings.narrativeMd: `DomainResource.modifierExtension` did not become a new element; it was already present and already a modifier. The important change is that it is now summary content. Implementers that use the StructureDefinition summary flag to shape REST `_summary` responses, generated classes, projection schemas, or cache keys should expect different summary payloads in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an old-valid/new-invalid instance break. The same full JSON/XML instance can carry `modifierExtension` in both R4 and R6. The compatibility issue is runtime behavior: summary views, strict summary DTOs, or clients that assume R4 summary fields may see an additional safety-significant element in R6.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update serializers and generated summary models to include `modifierExtension` for DomainResource-derived resources in R6 summary contexts. Add regression tests for summary responses containing resource-level modifier extensions and verify that clients either process or explicitly reject unknown modifier extensions rather than silently ignoring them.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably justified because modifier extensions can invert or qualify the meaning of resource content. A fully backward-compatible alternative would have been to keep the R4 flag and rely on narrative guidance, but that would leave summary behavior less computable and more likely to omit safety-relevant data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 changes only the `isSummary` flag for `DomainResource.modifierExtension`; the path, cardinality, type, slicing, and modifier status remain the same. A summary-mode response or generated summary DTO may now include resource-level modifier extensions where an R4 summary would not, but this is an additive summary-surface change rather than an R4 instance-validity break. Because modifier extensions are explicitly non-ignorable, including them in summaries is also a reasonable safety-oriented metadata choice.
keyEvidence: R6 `DomainResource.modifierExtension` keeps `0..* Extension` and `isModifier=true`, but has `isSummary=true`.
R4 maturity map and both StructureDefinitions mark DomainResource normative/FMM 5.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative/FMM 5 raised the bar for checking runtime summary behavior, but the change is additive metadata about summary projection and does not invalidate or remove any R4 content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling with limited runtime/API behavior: `_summary` serializers, caches, or summary DTOs may expose one more existing element, but base instance validation is unaffected.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `isSummary=false` and used prose saying summary producers should include modifier extensions. That would preserve the R4 summary shape, but it would be less computable and would undercut the safety goal of not dropping meaning-changing extensions from summaries.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identified possible summary-client churn and a partial prose alternative, but the fresh review rates the practical compatibility concern lower than Medium because this is additive summary metadata.

findings.title: Contained-resource invariant dom-3 was rewritten in FHIRPath

oldState.summary: R4 dom-3 required contained resources to be referenced or to refer to the container, with an expression that explicitly mentioned descendant `reference`, `canonical`, `uri`, and `url` values.

constraints.human: If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource
constraints.expression: contained.where((('#'+id in (%resource.descendants().reference | %resource.descendants().as(canonical) | %resource.descendants().as(uri) | %resource.descendants().as(url))) or descendants().where(reference = '#').exists() or descendants().where(as(canonical) = '#').exists() or descendants().where(as(canonical) = '#').exists()).not()).trace('unmatched', id).empty()

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 expression explicitly searched several primitive reference-like types and also allowed a contained resource to refer back to its container with `#`.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same dom-3 severity and human rule but rewrites the FHIRPath using `id.trace('id')`, `select(reference | as(uri))`, and `reference='#' | as(uri)='#'`.

constraints.human: If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource
constraints.expression: contained.where((('#'+id.trace('id') in %resource.descendants().select(reference | as(uri))) or descendants().where(reference='#' | as(uri)='#').exists()).not()).trace('unmatched', id).empty()

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 human-readable rule is unchanged, but the computable expression is not textually equivalent to R4. It relies on newer FHIRPath idioms and casting behavior.

facts.oldValue: If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource
facts.newValue: If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource

facts.oldValue: contained.where((('#'+id in (%resource.descendants().reference | %resource.descendants().as(canonical) | %resource.descendants().as(uri) | %resource.descendants().as(url))) or descendants().where(reference = '#').exists() or descendants().where(as(canonical) = '#').exists() or descendants().where(as(canonical) = '#').exists()).not()).trace('unmatched', id).empty()
facts.newValue: contained.where((('#'+id.trace('id') in %resource.descendants().select(reference | as(uri))) or descendants().where(reference='#' | as(uri)='#').exists()).not()).trace('unmatched', id).empty()
facts.note: The invariant is still an error-level DomainResource rule, but the FHIRPath was rewritten.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The finding compares the same constraint key (`dom-3`) on the same root element with unchanged human text and severity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: If the R6 expression is semantically equivalent under the intended R6 FHIRPath type system, there is no instance break. If implementations differ in how `as(uri)` handles `canonical`, `url`, or other reference-like primitives, a contained resource that passed R4 dom-3 could fail or pass differently in R6 validation. The risk is concentrated in resources whose contained resources are linked through canonical/uri/url-style fields rather than ordinary `Reference.reference`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The rule prevents orphaned contained resources. Divergent validation could reject valid migration data or miss an orphaned contained resource, but the affected pattern is likely uncommon.

justification.inferredGoal: Modernize and simplify the contained-resource reference invariant using R6 FHIRPath behavior.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 `dom-3` FHIRPath expression in the R6 base definition while clarifying intended semantics, if it remains valid under R6 FHIRPath.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The human `dom-3` rule and severity are unchanged, so the goal appears to be expression modernization rather than a deliberate stricter rule. A less-breaking base design exists, but it is only partial because the old expression may be buggy or outdated and official equivalence evidence is absent. Given the potential break is edge-case validator behavior rather than a clear structural instance break, the rewrite is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would be to retain the R4 expression for `dom-3` in R6, or make only minimal edits required for R6 FHIRPath validity while keeping explicit `reference`, `canonical`, `uri`, and `url` handling. This would preserve old validator behavior better, but it could carry forward the duplicated, cumbersome expression and fail to align with R6's preferred `as(uri)` model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining the old expression reduces validator churn but may preserve duplicated or outdated FHIRPath idioms and may not match the R6 type model.

evidence.detail: R4 dom-3 explicitly searches descendant reference, canonical, uri, and url values.
R6 dom-3 uses `select(reference | as(uri))` and `reference='#' | as(uri)='#'` instead.

examples.examplesMd: Regression examples should include contained resources referenced by ordinary `Reference.reference`, by canonical/uri/url-like fields when legal for the concrete resource, and by a contained resource that points back to its container using `#`. The exact JSON depends on a concrete DomainResource subtype and was not asserted here as a complete valid instance.

findings.narrativeMd: `dom-3` is a local DomainResource invariant, so its expression matters to every DomainResource subtype with contained resources. R6 did not change the rule text, but it did change the executable FHIRPath. Implementers that have custom validators or FHIRPath engines should not assume equivalence without tests.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This can be an old-valid/new-invalid or new-valid/old-invalid validation difference only for edge cases in contained-resource linking. Ordinary contained resources referenced through `Reference.reference` should remain aligned. The uncertain area is how engines evaluate the new `as(uri)`-based expression for canonical, url, uri, and related primitive values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Add validator regression tests for resources with contained entries. Include one case for each supported link mechanism, and run the tests with both R4 and R6 definitions. If differences appear, decide whether the migration should rewrite internal references, reject ambiguous contained resources, or apply a compatibility profile.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change appears aimed at expressing the same rule more cleanly. A backward-compatible path would have kept the R4 expression or published an official equivalence test suite. The tradeoff is that the old expression contained duplication and may not align with the R6 FHIRPath type model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should focus on whether R6 FHIRPath `as(uri)` is intended to subsume the R4 explicit `as(canonical)`, `as(uri)`, and `as(url)` checks in all relevant contexts.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The `dom-3` human rule and error severity are unchanged: contained resources still must be referenced from the containing resource or refer back to it. The R6 FHIRPath rewrites explicit `canonical`, `uri`, and `url` handling into `as(uri)`, and local type evidence shows `canonical` and `url` derive from `uri` in both R4 and R6. I do not see a credible intended old-valid/new-invalid change at the DomainResource path; this is best treated as a validator regression-test item for the expression rewrite rather than a standards compatibility problem.
keyEvidence: R4 and R6 `constraint[key=dom-3]` both have severity `error` and the same human text.
R4 expression checks descendant `reference`, `canonical`, `uri`, and `url` values; R6 expression uses `select(reference | as(uri))` and `as(uri)='#'`.
R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition-canonical` and `StructureDefinition-url` both have `baseDefinition` `StructureDefinition/uri`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative/FMM 5 means an actual error-invariant tightening would be serious, but the evidence points to an equivalent or slightly generalized expression of the same invariant rather than a new conformance rule.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: none for intended base conformance: the computable expression changed, so individual FHIRPath engines should be tested, but the underlying validation rule and uri-derived type coverage are preserved.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping the old expression would reduce textual churn, but it would preserve a bulkier, partly duplicated expression and would not provide a materially more compatible base rule once R6 uses `as(uri)` for uri-derived primitives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing potential hard/Medium impact as an action judgment; I agree only that validator behavior around the rewritten expression is worth regression testing.

findings.title: Local DomainResource invariants no longer include XPath expressions

oldState.summary: R4 local dom-* constraints included XPath expressions as well as FHIRPath expressions.

constraints.human: If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT contain nested Resources
If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource
If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a meta.versionId or a meta.lastUpdated
If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a security label
A resource should have narrative for robust management

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 root `DomainResource` constraints carried XPath metadata such as `not(parent::f:contained and f:contained)` for dom-2 and `exists(f:text/h:div)` for dom-6.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the local dom-* constraints but omits `constraint.xpath`; FHIRPath remains the computable expression.

constraints.human: If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT contain nested Resources
If the resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL be referred to from elsewhere in the resource or SHALL refer to the containing resource
If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a meta.versionId or a meta.lastUpdated
If a resource is contained in another resource, it SHALL NOT have a security label
A resource should have narrative for robust management

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 constraints include `source` references and FHIRPath expressions but no XPath fields.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same local DomainResource constraint keys are present in both versions; the removed metadata is the XPath representation attached to those local constraints.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR instances are not made invalid merely because XPath metadata is absent from the StructureDefinition. The risk is for validators, schema generators, documentation generators, or XML-specific tooling that consumed `constraint.xpath` rather than `constraint.expression`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If an XML validator silently stops enforcing dom-* rules because it only understands XPath, orphaned or invalid contained resources might be missed. The safer migration is to fail loudly or implement FHIRPath support.

justification.inferredGoal: Use FHIRPath as the primary computable invariant language and avoid maintaining duplicate XPath expressions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `constraint.xpath` as deprecated, non-authoritative transitional metadata while making FHIRPath authoritative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of FHIRPath-only invariant execution is reasonable, and no FHIR instance becomes invalid solely because XPath metadata is absent. However, immediate removal was not necessary to make FHIRPath authoritative. Retaining deprecated XPath metadata would have preserved R4-era XML validators and code generators at moderate maintenance cost, so this metadata break was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design would retain the existing XPath strings on the DomainResource dom-* constraints, or retain the `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath` slot globally, marked deprecated and non-authoritative. New or changed constraints could still require FHIRPath support. This would not solve long-term XPath retirement, but it would preserve most R4-era XPath-only tooling during transition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Requires duplicate constraint-language metadata and risks inconsistency, but for the existing local dom-* constraints the tradeoff is moderate and preserves XPath-only tooling.

evidence.detail: R4 dom-2 through dom-6 constraints each include an XPath expression.
R6 dom-2 through dom-6 constraints do not include `xpath`; they include FHIRPath `expression` and `source`.

examples.examplesMd: This finding has no JSON instance fragment because the break is in validator/code generator metadata. A representative failure mode is an XML validation pipeline that reads only `constraint.xpath`; after upgrading to R6 definitions it would have no local XPath rule to execute for dom-2 through dom-6.

findings.narrativeMd: The local DomainResource dom-* invariants still exist, so this is not a semantic deletion of the rules. It is a representation/tooling change: consumers must use FHIRPath rather than XPath to enforce them from the R6 StructureDefinition.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Full FHIRPath-aware validators can continue to enforce the constraints. XPath-only validators can lose executable constraints unless they are updated. This is therefore a runtime compatibility risk, not a direct R4-instance validation break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory validation tooling for any dependence on `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath`. Move DomainResource invariant execution to FHIRPath, and treat missing XPath as an explicit unsupported condition rather than silently skipping containment and narrative checks.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The backward-compatible alternative was straightforward: leave the XPath metadata in place. The likely tradeoff is that R6 would continue to carry a secondary constraint language that may not be equally expressive or equally maintained.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 removes the XPath form of the local `dom-*` constraints while retaining FHIRPath expressions. That does not make ordinary DomainResource instances invalid, but it is a real tooling break for XML/Schematron-era validators or generators that consumed `constraint.xpath` from the DomainResource StructureDefinition instead of executing FHIRPath. The break appears proportionate because R4 already described XPath as not useful for non-XML formats and warned it might be removed, and R6 keeps the cross-format expression language.
keyEvidence: R4 `DomainResource` constraints `dom-2` through `dom-6` each include an `xpath` string.
R6 keeps `dom-2` through `dom-6` but omits `xpath` and supplies FHIRPath `expression` plus `source`.
R4 `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath` comment says XPath is generally not useful for JSON and other formats and may be removed in the future.
R6 `ElementDefinition` no longer has `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath`, while `constraint.expression` remains.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative/FMM 5 increases concern for tooling that validates core resource invariants, but the removed representation was legacy metadata with an explicit R4 deprecation warning and an available FHIRPath replacement.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: XPath-only validators, Schematron generators, or code generators can no longer rely on `constraint.xpath`; instance wire compatibility is not directly affected.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 design could have retained `constraint.xpath` as deprecated, non-authoritative metadata. That would help legacy XML tooling, but it would keep duplicate constraint languages in the base model, risk divergence from FHIRPath, and delay the cross-format cleanup.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identified a real tooling break and a plausible retained-XPath alternative, but I view the removal as proportionate rather than a change needing renewed DomainResource design attention.

findings.title: Contained-resource text now calls out Parameters and additional resources

oldState.summary: `contained` was `0..* Resource` with text describing resources that have no independent existence or transaction scope.

semanticText.definition: These resources do not have an independent existence apart from the resource that contains them - they cannot be identified independently, and nor can they have their own independent transaction scope.
semanticText.comment: This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags In their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not specifically call out `Parameters` resources or additional resources in the `contained` element definition/comment.

newState.summary: `contained` remains `0..* Resource`, but the definition says Parameters is allowed only when referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning, and the comment mentions additional resources.

semanticText.definition: These resources do not have an independent existence apart from the resource that contains them - they cannot be identified independently, nor can they have their own independent transaction scope. This is allowed to be a Parameters resource if and only if it is referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning.
semanticText.comment: This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags in their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels. Contained resources may be a resource type defined in the FHIR specification, or an [additional resource](resource.html#additional).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds semantically important text for `Parameters` and for resources outside the main resource set, while leaving the computable type as `Resource`.

facts.newValue: Parameters is allowed if and only if referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning.
Contained resources may be a FHIR specification resource type or an additional resource.

facts.note: The computable type domain did not change at this element.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same local element id and path are present with unchanged cardinality and type; the material delta is definition/comment text.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The StructureDefinition does not add a new computable target profile or invariant for this text, so ordinary validators may not reject instances solely on this basis. However, the words `if and only if` can affect conformance review for contained `Parameters`, and `additional resource` support creates a conversion concern because R4 systems may not know R6-only or additional resource types inside `contained`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is mostly interoperability and conversion policy. It could matter clinically if a contained Parameters resource supplies context that a receiver drops or cannot interpret.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify when Parameters and additional resources may be contained.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 permissive base wording and add R6 guidance or examples, or phrase the Parameters text as non-normative guidance rather than an if-and-only-if base rule.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying contained `Parameters` and additional resources is a reasonable goal, but the StructureDefinitions alone do not show whether R6 intended a new conformance rule or merely clarified existing practice. The additional-resource sentence is mostly an R6-to-R4 conversion concern, while the `Parameters` if-and-only-if wording could affect R4-to-R6 conformance review. Because the less-breaking text alternative only fully meets a clarification goal, not a firm base-policy goal, the alternative is partial and the verdict remains unassessable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would preserve the R4 definition's permissive structure and add examples or a clearly non-normative comment that contained `Parameters` need context and that additional resources may need conversion policy. That would protect R4 instances that used contained `Parameters` without an explicit contextual reference, but it would not provide the same clear base conformance statement as the R6 `if and only if` wording.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids semantic churn for existing contained Parameters, but weaker base wording may leave implementers without a clear interoperable policy for Parameters and additional resources.

evidence.detail: R4 describes contained resources but does not mention Parameters.
R6 adds that contained Parameters is allowed if and only if referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning.
R6 says contained resources may be a resource type defined in the FHIR specification or an additional resource.

examples.examplesMd: An R6 DomainResource-derived instance that contains `Parameters` or an R6 additional resource needs policy review before conversion to R4. If the contained resource type is unknown to the R4 receiver, the content may require an extension, Binary/document packaging, a profile-specific transform, or rejection.

findings.narrativeMd: `DomainResource.contained` did not change structurally, but its conformance text did. R6 explicitly discusses contained `Parameters` and additional resources. That can affect reviewers, validators with narrative-aware rules, and cross-version converters even when base cardinality and type are unchanged.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no new computable cardinality, type, or target-profile restriction in the element itself. The potential break is semantic: R4 content with contained `Parameters` might require extra justification under R6, and R6 content with additional or R6-only contained resource types may not be directly representable for R4 receivers.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Flag contained `Parameters` and contained resource types not known to R4 during migration. Confirm that each contained resource is referenced and has clear context/meaning. For R6-only resource types, define an explicit conversion strategy rather than relying on generic contained-resource passthrough.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: If the intent was only clarification, a non-normative note would have been less disruptive. If the intent was to define a firm policy for `Parameters`, placing it in the base element text is more discoverable but leaves enforcement partly manual because the StructureDefinition does not encode a concrete invariant.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Narrative spec pages would help decide whether this is a new conformance requirement or a clarification of existing practice.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The computable shape of `DomainResource.contained` is unchanged at `0..* Resource`, but R6 adds absolute prose saying a contained `Parameters` resource is allowed if and only if it is referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning, and adds text about additional resources. The Parameters sentence could be read as enforceable base conformance beyond ordinary structural validation, while the additional-resource sentence is mostly R6 expressiveness and downgrade policy. Without official rationale or validator behavior, it is not defensible to decide whether this is merely clarification, a new prose-only restriction, or a meaningful compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 `DomainResource.contained` is `0..* Resource` with no Parameters-specific sentence.
R6 `DomainResource.contained` remains `0..* Resource` and adds: `This is allowed to be a Parameters resource if and only if it is referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning.`
R6 comment adds that contained resources may be a FHIR specification resource type or an additional resource.
`Parameters` derives from `Resource` in both the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative/FMM 5 makes ambiguous conformance prose on a base element worth attention, especially because `contained` is inherited broadly by DomainResource resources.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: ordinary validators see the same type and cardinality, but stricter conformance review could reject context-free contained Parameters; R6-to-R4 loss is possible for R6 additional resource types.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have used softer guidance, examples, a warning-level rule, or profile-specific policy for contained Parameters. Those alternatives would preserve more legacy interpretation, but they may not meet the R6 goal if the intent is a firm base rule for context-bearing Parameters.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report appropriately treated the impact and alternative as uncertain/partial; the fresh review follows the framework's approach for this kind of Parameters prose change and leaves the final action judgment as Unclear.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, abstract flag, type, baseDefinition, and derivation are unchanged. Version/package metadata changed as expected for R6 ballot4.
The local elements `text`, `contained`, `extension`, and `modifierExtension` are present in both R4 and R6. No local element removal, addition, rename, move, split, or merge was found.
`DomainResource.text` remains `0..1`; `contained`, `extension`, and `modifierExtension` remain `0..*`; the root remains `0..*`.
`text` remains `Narrative`, `contained` remains `Resource`, and both extension elements remain `Extension`.
No local DomainResource element is a `Reference` with target profiles, and no local reference target change was found.
The local DomainResource elements have no terminology bindings. The inherited `Resource.language` binding change is out of scope.
No fixed, pattern, or default value was found on the local DomainResource elements in either version.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraint change was found.
`modifierExtension` remains `isModifier=true`; the root, `text`, `contained`, and `extension` remain non-modifier elements. The summary flag change for `modifierExtension` is reported separately.
`extension` and `modifierExtension` retain open slicing by `url`. No local slicing discriminator, ordered flag, or rule change was found.

The local structural elements are representable in R4 because no local element or type was added. The remaining R6-to-R4 concerns are summary behavior, `contained` semantic text, and concrete R6 resource types handled outside this artifact.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds condition back-links from local elements to existing dom-* constraints
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds `condition` metadata such as `DomainResource.text` pointing to `dom-6` and `DomainResource.contained` pointing to `dom-2`, `dom-3`, `dom-4`, and `dom-5`. The underlying constraints already existed on the root in R4, so this is not a new validation rule by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and code generators may now display these elements as explicitly affected by root constraints. Do not treat the metadata alone as a new cardinality or type restriction.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records mustSupport=false where R4 commonly omitted it
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 includes explicit `mustSupport:false` on the local DomainResource elements. In the base StructureDefinition this is equivalent to the absent/default false value in R4 and does not create support obligations.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators that distinguish missing from false should normalize both to false for base-definition comparison.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Extension ext-1 is no longer repeated on DomainResource extension elements in the same way
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 repeated the `ext-1` Extension constraint on the DomainResource `extension` and `modifierExtension` elements. R6 still defines `ext-1` on the `Extension` datatype itself, so this is best treated as an inherited Extension/tooling placement issue rather than a local DomainResource content-model change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validators should enforce Extension's own constraints when validating DomainResource extension children. The Extension artifact report should own any breaking assessment of `ext-1` placement or Extension value[x] changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Inherited `Resource` elements appear in the DomainResource snapshot and include material-looking changes such as `Resource.language` binding details. They are out of scope here and should be assessed in the Resource report.
`DomainResource.extension` and `DomainResource.modifierExtension` keep type `Extension`, while inherited Extension constraints and value[x] type-domain changes are owned by the Extension artifact.

R6 `DomainResource.contained` text mentions additional resources. Cross-version conversion risk depends on which concrete R6 resources are absent from R4 and whether they may appear in contained form.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 DomainResource diff, change proposal, or Jira rationale was available. Justification and backward-compatible alternative analysis are inferred from the StructureDefinitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use an official HL7 diff/change log or ballot reconciliation notes explaining the DomainResource changes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The `dom-3` assessment did not execute an official FHIRPath conformance test suite across R4 and R6 engines. The reported impact is therefore a potential validator-divergence risk rather than a proven behavioral difference.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run official validator test cases for contained resources, especially references through `Reference`, `canonical`, `url`, and `uri`-typed fields.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative specification pages were not used as primary evidence. They may clarify whether the contained `Parameters` and additional-resource wording is a new conformance requirement or an editorial clarification.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the R4 and R6 DomainResource/resource narrative pages and any linked additional-resource guidance.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No local DomainResource terminology bindings were present. Terminology expansion was therefore not material to the local report, but inherited Resource terminology changes require separate analysis.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Consult the Resource artifact report and terminology expansions for inherited `Resource.language`.
